full_judgment:
2. Brief facts giving rise to this Rule are that, the petitioner is a proprietor of Islam Ship Builders and Heavy Engineering and one of the very few private organisations working with Bangladesh Railway. When Bangladesh Railway became a losing concern the Government decided to privatise all the trains except the Inter City Classes. Under that scheme of privatisation the petitioner took lease of 10 trains running in different routes. On 17-7-2002 Bangladesh Railway invited tender by publishing a notice and the petitioner participated in the tender in respect of train Nos. 41/42 (Kanchan Express) running on the route of Parbatipur- Thakurgaon-Parbatipur and 513/514, 505/506, 507/508 (another group) local trains running on the route of Paradaha-Goalanda Ghat-Paradaha. It was specified in the tender notice that the prospective bidders may drop their schedules in three different places, namely, (1) CTM/ West, Bangladesh Railway, Rajshahi, (2) Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi and (3) Joint Director General (PM), Bangladesh Railway, Room No. 508, Rail Bhaban, 16 Abdul Gani Road, Dhaka. Accordingly, the petitioner and others participated in the bid for both the groups. There were 3 and 5 bidders for the first group and second group of trains respectively including the petitioner. On 11-8-2002 at about 11-45 AM the petitioner dropped his schedules in the box stationed in the Office of the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi and after scrutiny of all the tenders the petitioner became the highest bidder for both the groups of trains. On 11-8-2002 one Md Nazrul Islam, proprietor of Banna Enterprise, who also participated for both the groups of said trains, dropped his tender schedule in Dhaka office and he wrote a letter to the respondent No. 2, copy of which was sent to the Deputy Minister for Communication and respondent No. 3 complaining that apparently the petitioner dropped his tender at 12-30 PM only after knowing his rate over the mobile telephone. The other participants of the bid also made complaint making the same allegations. On 21-8-2002 respondent No. 6, Deputy Director/ TC, Bangladesh Railway ordered for an investigation about the allegations made by the other bidders including the said Banna Enterprise and thereafter the Assistant Chief Commercial Manager/R/ West on behalf of the respondent No. 5 vide letter bearing Memo No. COM/RCS/L/41-42 /CRD-2/Pa: and COM/ RCS/L/506-506/ CRD-2/ Pa: informed that both the aforesaid tenders have been cancelled. It is alleged by the petitioner that the cancellation was made without assigning any reason and serving any notice upon the petitioner. Thereafter, on 26-8-2002 the petitioner appealed to the Hon'ble Minister for Communication for his intervention in this matter. The Hon'ble Minister asked the respondent No. 2, Director General, Bangladesh Railway to make an inquiry into the matter and take necessary action. Following the direction the respondent No. 2 asked the Additional Deputy Director (Operation) and respondent No. 3 to inquire into the matter. On 24-9-2002 the inquiry committee submitted its detailed report where none of the allegations made by the other bidders were found to be true and the inquiry committee also confirmed that the petitioner was the highest bidder in both the tenders and there was no malpractice in the said bidding process. By letter dated 17-10-2002 the Deputy Director, Local Government, Rajshahi Division also confirmed that there has been no irregularity in the tender of both the groups of trains in which the petitioner became the highest bidder. The petitioner claims that in the note sheet of the relevant file it has been clearly mentioned that there was no irregularities on the part of the petitioner and the concerned authority and it will reveal from the note sheet that it was recommended by the highest authority to grant license to the petitioner for both the groups. The respondent No. 5 Chief Traffic Manager (West) ignoring the reports of the inquiry committee and also the direction made by the highest authority arbitrarily and abruptly published another advertisement in the Daily Sangbad dated 8-2-2003 inviting fresh tender for the aforesaid two groups of trains and cancelled the bid by order dated 21-8-2002 (Annexure E and E1) which are also impugned in this writ petition. 

 3. The respondent No. 4 General Manager (West) has filed affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the Bangladesh Railway invited tender from the private sector through different newspapers for train No. 41/42 Kanchan Express and 513/514, 505/ 506, 507/508 local trains. The date of sale of tender schedule was fixed on 30-7-2002-10-8-2002 and on 11-8-2002 at 12-00 noon on the same day 8 other participants participated in the tender and dropped their tender at different places as specified in the tender. Thereafter 3 bidders filed complaint stating that the tender schedule was dropped in the Head Office; Dhaka which was opened at 12-15 to 12-45 PM, the Islam Ship Builders did not submit his tender schedule in the Office of the Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi. Thereafter, an inquiry was held by the authority and it was found that the allegation was not proved but just for fair administration the authority cancelled the bid. It has further been contended that in Clause 5 of the tender schedule there is a provision to the effect that “চুক্তি পত্রে স্বাক্ষরের পূর্বে যে কোন সময় যে কোন পর্য্যায়ে এই প্রক্রিয়া স্থগিত বা বাতিল করার প্রক্রিয়া রেলওয়ে কর্তৃপক্ষের থাকিবে। কোন কারণ দর্শানো ব্যতিরেকে রেলওয়ে কর্তৃক যে কোন দরপত্র গ্রহন বা বাতিল করিতে পারিবে।” 

 4. Mr Abdul Matin Khasru, the learned Counsel, contended that the petitioner became the highest bidder and the petitioner's bid having been accepted by the authority and ultimately, that was on further verification and assessment approved by the highest authority of the department, the respondent No. 5 had no authority to issue the impugned notice dated 8-2-2003 inviting fresh tender cancelling the bid by impugned order dated 21-8-2002 (Annexures E and E1). He has further argued that the cancellation of the bid by the respondent is arbitrary and such action is sheer highhandedness of the subordinate executive authority since the matter has been finally resolved by the highest authority of the department and that highest authority got the approval of the Minister after verification and inquiry and, as such, the fresh tender notice dated 8-2-2003 purported to have been issued by the respondent No. 5, the Chief Traffic Manager, Bangladesh Railway, is malafide, arbitrary and that was issued at the instigation of the interested quarter, otherwise the petitioner would have got the licence according to the decision of the Communication Minister and the highest authority of the department concerned.
